articles.title: Trump niega un ataque contra Irán antes de las elecciones, pero el Pentágono prepara opciones de combate
articles.summary: Una nueva ofensiva contra Irán podría convertirse en un salvavidas electoral para Netanyahu y Trump, pero también en una trampa si dispara el precio del petróleo y prolonga la guerra. El analista Carlos Novoa advierte: “lo que no puede ocurrir es que sea una guerra de alta intensidad permanente”
articles.body_text: La posibilidad de una nueva escalada entre Estados Unidos e Irán quedó en suspenso después de que Donald Trump asegurara el jueves que no atacará la República Islámica antes de las elecciones de medio mandato. La declaración se produce luego de que medios estadounidenses revelaran que el Pentágono prepara opciones militares para reanudar las operaciones contra Irán, incluso antes de los comicios estadonidenses y los de Israel. ¿Qué hay detrás de esta aparente contradicción y qué papel juega el calendario electoral en los cálculos de Washington y Jerusalén? Israel irá a elecciones legislativas el 27 de octubre, donde el primer ministro Benjamin Netanyahu se juega su continuidad en el poder en una contienda muy ajustada y sin un bloque con mayoría asegurada. Mientras tanto, los comicios de medio mandato en Estados Unidos se celebrarán el 3 de noviembre, con un escenario adverso para los republicanos, que enfrentan el riesgo de perder el control de una o incluso ambas cámaras del Congreso, lo que dificultaría los dos años de gestión que le quedan al presidente. Trump reaccionó el jueves a las últimas noticias y afirmó que no iniciará ataques contra Irán “en ningún momento antes de las elecciones de medio mandato”. También afirmó que Washington está manteniendo conversaciones “productivas” con Teherán y describió la situación de Irán como “muy delicada” tanto económica como militarmente mientras mantiene el bloqueo al petróleo iraní en el estrecho de Ormuz. La declaración de Trump contrasta con los preparativos militares revelados en las últimas horas. Según Axios, el Pentágono ordenó hace varios días al Comando Central de Estados Unidos (CENTCOM) que concluyera los planes para una eventual reanudación de las principales operaciones de combate en Irán. El medio remarcó que la directiva no incluía una fecha específica para el lanzamiento de los ataques, y que Trump no ha tomado ninguna decisión definitiva. Sin embargo, fuentes estadounidenses e israelíes de Axios indicaron que podría ocurrir antes de las elecciones en Estados Unidos y, posiblemente, una semana antes de las de Israel. Axios indicó que las operaciones de combate incluirían bombardeos masivos contra objetivos nucleares, energéticos y de infraestructura iraníes. Además, Trump habló el miércoles con Netanyahu. Fue su segunda llamada entre ambos pocos días, anotó Axios. Por su parte, The Atlantic coincidió en que la Casa Blanca ha pedido al Pentágono que prepare opciones de ataque contra Irán que podrían ejecutarse antes del 3 de noviembre. La posibilidad de una operación antes de las elecciones responde, según los funcionarios citados por The Atlantic, a un doble interés de Trump: presionar a Irán para que avance hacia una negociación, y tratar de reducir los precios de la gasolina, que se han convertido en un problema político para los republicanos. The Atlantic remarcó que existe una fuerte corriente de cautela dentro del propio entorno republicano, pues la guerra es impopular en Estados Unidos y varios candidatos de ese partido consideran que el conflicto y el encarecimiento de la gasolina están perjudicando sus campañas. El riesgo militar también es considerable, advierte The Atlantic, porque una nueva ofensiva expondría a unos 50.000 militares estadounidenses desplegados en Medio Oriente a posibles represalias iraníes, además de poner en riesgo de nuevo a los aliados del Golfo y consumir más municiones estratégicas estadounidenses. The Atlantic informó que la Casa Blanca considera que Irán atraviesa su momento de mayor debilidad desde el inicio de la guerra el 28 de febrero, por el deterioro de su economía, la inflación y las divisiones dentro del liderazgo. Sin embargo, los sectores más duros del régimen parecen mantener una posición dominante y poco dispuesta a negociar. La posibilidad de una nueva escalada militar con Irán llega en un momento especialmente delicado para Netanyahu, que afrontará el 27 de octubre unas elecciones en las que su gestión de la crisis iniciada con el ataque de Hamás del 7 de octubre de 2023 estará nuevamente bajo escrutinio, advirtió el periodista y analista internacional Carlos Novoa. “Para Netanyahu, siempre los conflictos o guerras han sido tablas de salvación”, sostuvo Novoa. El analista precisó que una latente amenaza iraní que vaya más allá de las declaraciones podría terminar favoreciendo al primer ministro al activar uno de los resortes más poderosos de la política israelí: la necesidad de seguridad frente a una amenaza externa. “Una acción militar tiene el efecto de unificar a una población que lo que quiere es una respuesta y que su gobernante les dé algún tipo de seguridad”, remarcó. Sin embargo, Novoa consideró que un eventual beneficio electoral surgido del regreso a la guerra no garantiza la continuidad de Netanyahu. Insistió en que arrastra el cuestionamiento por las fallas de seguridad que permitieron el ataque de Hamás y por la gestión posterior de la crisis de los rehenes. Novoa consideró que Trump “ya asimiló que va a perder las elecciones de medio término. Pero también puede estar midiendo las consecuencias políticas de una nueva confrontación con Irán. El analista cree que, para justificar una nueva ofensiva, Washington necesitaría construir el relato de un Irán agresivo y peligroso. Pero advierte que el problema es que ese argumento es fácil neutralizar porque Teherán solo se está defendiendo, “ataca cuando lo atacan”. Novoa piensa que una eventual decisión de reanudar las operaciones militares podría tener un componente electoral tanto en Israel como en Estados Unidos, aunque los beneficios políticos no estarían asegurados. Calcula que el principal problema para Trump sería que una nueva ofensiva no produzca una victoria rápida y, en cambio, termine trasladando los costos de la guerra directamente al bolsillo de los estadounidenses. “La principal consecuencia sería el incremento del precio de los combustibles en todo el mundo y particularmente en los Estados Unidos”, advirtió. Ese es el punto en el que una estrategia pensada para obtener réditos políticos podría transformarse en un problema electoral, remarcó Novoa. “La población estadounidense puede tolerar una operación militar limitada, pero el efecto cambia si la guerra se traduce en gasolina más cara durante las semanas previas a las elecciones”. Novoa refiere que si Estados Unidos decide reanudar las operaciones contra Irán, tendría incentivos para que la nueva fase sea breve y de alta intensidad, evitando quedar atrapado en una guerra prolongada. “Estados Unidos sabe que una guerra de esta naturaleza no puede durar mucho tiempo”, indicó. Una nueva ofensiva podría extenderse alrededor de una semana, según su estimación, sin que eso signifique necesariamente el final del conflicto. Después podría abrirse una etapa de tensión y expectativa, pero con menor intensidad militar. El verdadero peligro aparecería si la escalada se convierte en una guerra de alta intensidad sostenida. La economía entonces podría generar un desgaste político mucho mayor para Trump, precisamente cuando los estadounidenses se preparan para votar. Una operación rápida podría permitir a Netanyahu presentarse como garante de la seguridad de Israel y a Trump proyectar fortaleza frente a Irán. Pero una guerra que se prolongue, dispare el precio del petróleo o provoque una respuesta iraní de mayor escala podría generar exactamente el efecto contrario, resume Novoa.

articles.summary: El calendario de feriados 2026 aún contempla varias fechas de descanso. Conoce cuántos feriados quedan en octubre y qué se conmemora en cada uno.
articles.body_text: Tras culminar las celebraciones respectivas, muchos trabajadores y estudiantes ya empiezan a revisar el calendario para conocer cuál será el siguiente descanso oficial del año. Los feriados representan una oportunidad para planificar viajes, compartir tiempo en familia o simplemente hacer una pausa en la rutina, por lo que existe un gran interés en conocer las próximas fechas establecidas por ley. Además de permitir un espacio para el descanso, estas jornadas suelen generar un importante movimiento en sectores como el turismo, el comercio, la gastronomía y el transporte, debido al incremento de personas que aprovechan los días libres para salir de la ciudad o realizar diversas actividades. Del mismo modo, muchas empresas y entidades organizan con anticipación sus operaciones para adecuarse al calendario oficial, mientras que las familias aprovechan estas fechas para programar reuniones, escapadas de fin de semana o visitas a distintos destinos del país. Por ello, conocer con anticipación cuándo será el próximo feriado resulta clave para organizar la agenda personal y laboral, evitar contratiempos y sacar el máximo provecho a los días de descanso que aún quedan en el 2026. A continuación, te contaremos todo lo que debes saber sobre esta situación. El mes de octubre cuenta con un feriado. Si quieres saber cuándo será el próximo feriado y qué fechas aún quedan por disfrutar este año, aquí te contamos todos los detalles. Los feriados son fechas establecidas por ley en las que los trabajadores tienen derecho a suspender sus labores sin que ello afecte su remuneración. Durante estas jornadas, el descanso es obligatorio tanto para el sector público como para el privado, salvo en aquellas actividades que, por su naturaleza, deben continuar operando. Si un trabajador presta servicios durante un feriado y no recibe un día de descanso compensatorio, la legislación laboral establece que le corresponde una remuneración adicional por haber laborado en esa fecha, conforme a las disposiciones vigentes. A diferencia del feriado, el día no laborable no constituye un descanso obligatorio para todos los trabajadores. Generalmente, esta medida se aplica al sector público con el objetivo de extender periodos de descanso o promover actividades como el turismo interno. En el caso de las entidades públicas, las horas que no se trabajan deben recuperarse posteriormente, dentro del plazo fijado por la normativa o según lo disponga cada institución. Para el sector privado, la aplicación de un día no laborable depende de un acuerdo entre empleador y trabajadores. Si no existe consenso sobre la recuperación de las horas, será el empleador quien determine la forma en que estas deberán compensarse.

articles.title: Cusco: Serfor capacitará a más de 400 brigadistas para prevenir incendios forestales
articles.summary: El Serfor inició un programa de capacitación para formar a más de 400 brigadistas en 26 distritos de Cusco durante octubre. Además, brindará asistencia técnica a autoridades de 101 distritos para fortalecer el uso de alertas tempranas y la prevención de incendios forestales.
articles.body_text: El Servicio Nacional Forestal y de Fauna Silvestre (Serfor) inició la capacitación de brigadistas locales en Cusco con la meta de formar a más de 400 personas durante octubre, como parte de las acciones de prevención de incendios forestales en la región. Las actividades se desarrollarán en 26 distritos identificados por su mayor incidencia de estas emergencias. La formación comenzó en el distrito de Poroy, en la provincia de Cusco, con la participación de 22 brigadistas. Un equipo de 14 profesionales de la Dirección General de Información y Ordenamiento Forestal y de Fauna Silvestre del Serfor, procedente de Lima, está a cargo de las jornadas. “Se han focalizado 26 distritos en los que se darán 21 capacitaciones certificadas durante el mes de octubre. La meta es formar en territorio a más de 400 brigadistas, los cuales se sumarán a los 131 que capacitamos en el año pasado”, señaló Robert Camero Villasante, responsable de la Administración Técnica Forestal y de Fauna Silvestre (ATFFS) Cusco del Serfor. La iniciativa se desarrolla en coordinación con el Centro de Operaciones de Emergencia Regional (COER) de Cusco y las autoridades locales. Según la entidad, los brigadistas contribuirán a las labores de prevención y servirán de apoyo a las instituciones encargadas de responder ante los incendios forestales. El Serfor también brindará asistencia técnica y capacitaciones a autoridades y trabajadores de municipalidades distritales y provinciales sobre el uso del Sistema de Alerta Temprana, que emplea información de focos de calor para facilitar la toma de decisiones. De acuerdo con Camero, estas actividades se realizarán en 101 distritos de las 13 provincias de Cusco, con una cobertura prevista del 88 % del territorio regional. Las acciones forman parte de la campaña “Prevenir un incendio forestal cuesta menos que combatirlo”, mediante la cual el Serfor exhorta a la población rural a evitar las quemas agrícolas y de rastrojos sin control, no dejar fogatas encendidas y reportar oportunamente cualquier indicio de incendio a las autoridades. La institución también señaló que continuará con las labores de monitoreo y alerta temprana para verificar la evolución de estas emergencias y contribuir a una respuesta oportuna de las entidades competentes, con el objetivo de proteger los recursos forestales y la fauna silvestre.

Si un trabajador presta servicios durante un feriado y no recibe un día de descanso compensatorio, la legislación laboral establece que le corresponde una remuneración adicional por haber laborado en esa fecha, conforme a las disposiciones vigentes. A diferencia del feriado, el día no laborable no constituye un descanso obligatorio para todos los trabajadores. Generalmente, esta medida se aplica al sector público con el objetivo de extender periodos de descanso o promover actividades como el turismo interno. En el caso de las entidades públicas, las horas que no se trabajan deben recuperarse posteriormente, dentro del plazo fijado por la normativa o según lo disponga cada institución. Para el sector privado, la aplicación de un día no laborable depende de un acuerdo entre empleador y trabajadores. Si no existe consenso sobre la recuperación de las horas, será el empleador quien determine la forma en que estas deberán compensarse.

En ese sentido, cuestionó la actividad de la minería ilegal y sostuvo que esta “recurre a la violencia para apropiarse ilícitamente de zonas de trabajo y recursos minerales”. Añadió que lo ocurrido evidencia la gravedad de una actividad que, según afirmó, amenaza la vida de las personas, la seguridad de la provincia y el Estado de Derecho. articles.title: Incendio forestal en Cusco: 278 reportes de fuego en la región, 8 mil hectáreas afectadas y bomberos que no se dan abasto
articles.summary: La nota abarca las causas del incendio forestal en Cusco, la labora de los bonberos de la zona, el accionar del gobierno regional de Cusco, pero también los impacto ambientales de este desastre.
articles.body_text: Las provincias de Canchis, Chumbivilcas y Espinar en la región Cusco son presas del fuego de seis incendios forestales activos provocados por el factor humano producto de tradiciones agrícolas como la “quema de tierra”. Los bomberos avanzan en la labor de contener las llamas pese a tremendas limitaciones logísticas. Entre el 26 de setiembre y el 2 de octubre, se han reportado cinco fallecidos, tres adultos mayores en los distritos de Yanahuara, Yanatile y Colquepata, y dos hermanos menores de edad de 11 y 18 años como consecuencia de fuertes quemaduras tras verse expuestos a las llamas. El Servicio Nacional de Meteorología e Hidrología (Senamhi) asegura que estos incendios tienen que ver, entre otras cosas, con las condiciones meteorológicas que atraviesa la sierra sur peruana. De hecho, aseguran haber emitido alertas sobre el aumento de temperaturas que vendrían con fuertes vientos, condiciones propicias para la expansión del fuego. Al respecto, Miguel Alejandro Oscco, director regional de la oficina de gestión de riesgo de desastres y seguridad de la región Cusco dice lo siguiente: “tenemos un escenario favorable para incendios forestales por la alta radiación solar, las altas temperaturas. Habitualmente es de 22 a 24 grados, pero hemos llegado hasta los 29. Es algo fuera de lo usual. Además, hay vegetación muy seca con heladas en la madrugada, la sequedad de la vegetación, los vientos a partir de las 11 de la mañana, lo normal es que se presenten recién entre las 3 a 4 de la tarde. Cualquier chispa puede iniciar un fuego que termina en un incendio forestal”. Victoria Villarrubia, directora de Perú Resiliente, en conversación con El Comercio, detalla: “el impacto fundamental es sobre la flora de la zona donde hay vegetación que sirve a modo de contención en épocas de lluvias para evitar huaicos, pero eso cambia cuando hay devastación por incendios dejando expuestos estos terrenos proclives a deslizamientos”. Sin embargo, de acuerdo a vecinos de la zona, los incendios en la región también tienen mucho que ver con antiguas costumbres agrarias como la quema de tierra, que no es otra cosa que prender fuego de forma intencional a un terreno para eliminar restos de cosecha anterior, maleza, plagas y vegetación. Pío Vásquez de Velasco, residente de Urubamba y propietario del restaurante El Huacatay, dice lo siguiente sobre dicha tradición: “todos los años empieza en setiembre (los incendios), muchos provocados por quemar la tierra para volver a sembrar. Si no tienen acceso (a maquinaria) es la forma más económica para hacerlo y la gente necesita la tierra para cultivar su chacra”. Versión confirmada por Oscco: “el 100% de los incendios de este año, como del año pasado, han sido generados por la mano del hombre, todos por quemas agrícolas. Algunos quieren renovar el pasto porque se envejece, que no se degrada fácilmente, entonces lo queman para que vuelva a brotar. Nuestros ancestros agarraban la tierra, la volteaban y el pasto brotaba por el otro lado, nuevo, renovado, pero es un proceso más largo, ellos quieren algo más rápido, por eso lo queman, pero con el viento y el sol el fuego se propaga rápidamente y pierden el control”. De hecho, Vásquez de Velasco agrega que no pocos de estos incidentes son provocados por personas de la tercera edad: “Al parecer, el señor murió en Yanahuara habría provocado el incendio, pero no se le quiere dar mucha visibilidad porque la comunidad protege su identidad”, palabras que fueron ratificadas por el funcionario de la región Cusco: “los 3 ancianos fallecidos realizaron quema de tierra”. Villarrubia indica que esta práctica es generalizada en todo el Perú y que su persistencia tiene una explicación: “no se informa lo suficiente a los campesinos. Tiene que haber información constante, de acompañar a los agricultores, pues hay mecanismos para reemplazar estos procesos, pero no se implementan por falta de conocimiento o también porque chocan con métodos tradicionales, culturales que se pasan de generación en generación y ahí entran los gobiernos locales”. El Comercio también conversó con el David Taboada, comandante de la IX Comandancia Departamental de Cusco del Cuerpo de Bomberos del Perú (CBP), compañía que se está haciendo cargo de controlar los seis incendios, pero con diversas dificultades que van desde la geografía, el equipamiento y el apoyo del Estado para realizar las respectivas labores. “Llegar al punto de incendio no es fácil porque no está a pie de carretera, sino encima de los cerros. Llega un punto donde la camioneta no puede avanzar más, entonces tenemos que caminar y el incendio no espera (...) Ahí hace falta articular esfuerzos con la Fuerza Aérea para que, con un helicóptero, nos movilicen hasta el punto”. En cuatro al equipamiento con que cuentan, Taboada confirmó el apoyo del gobierno regional del Cusco en cuanto a la dotación de 15 camionetas y equipos; sin embargo, detalló que los vehículos no tienen el mantenimiento debido y los equipos tienen que renovarse constantemente. “Estas herramientas ya están obsoletas porque se dañan en un solo incendio, urge renovarlas, lo mismo con los equipos de protección personal, las motobombas, las sopladoras que son vitales en incendios forestales. Nuestros recursos son insuficientes”. Asimismo, detalló que actualmente hay unos 30 bomberos haciendo los esfuerzos para controlar la situación, pero que este número es insuficiente: “se necesitan muchas cuadrillas, alrededor de 500 personas que estén entrenadas”, además apuntó a que, por lo general, los gobiernos locales no han conformado como se debe las respectivas brigadas: “no solo deben esperar a que lleguen los bomberos o la policía”, acotó. La región Cusco también ha realizado trabajos coordinados con el cuerpo de bomberos que está realizando las acciones de contención de fuego originado desde la semana pasada. Al respecto, Miguel Oscco comenta: “Hemos equipado a los bomberos con camionetas, equipos de extinción rápida, de extinción de forestales, hemos tenido hasta dos proyectos con ellos y apuntamos a un tercer proyecto para fortalecer las capacidades de respuesta, para dotarlos con lo que necesiten”. Sin embargo, no solo los bomberos se han movilizado, también vecinos de la zona, así también organizaciones como es el caso de Vidawasi, una organización sin fines de lucro ubicada en el Valle Sagrado de los Incas, la cual realizó coordinaciones con la Fuerza Aérea del Perú (FAP) para gestionar la llegada a la zona de un helicóptero que se encargue de transportar agua desde el río Vilcanota para ayudar a controlar el avance del fuego. Oscco comenta que es el Servicio Nacional Forestal y de Fauna Silvestre (SERFOR) el encargado del control de incendios forestales, el cual posee un plan de acción nacional aprobado en 2025. pero que al no contar con brigadistas el trabajo de esta se ve muy limitado, por lo que termina siendo la región Cusco la responsable de realizar dichas acciones. “Hemos avanzado bastante a nivel de inversión de prevención de incendios forestales logrando capacitar a las municipalidades, adoptar equipamiento, la formación de brigadistas. Pese a que somos gobierno regional tenemos trabajo como gobierno local trabajando y fortaleciendo a las comunidades. Pero, lo más importante es buscar la prevención”. En ese sentido, detalló que cuando se producen este tipo de emergencias cuentan con un comité regional donde también participa SERFOR, pero también el Ministerio Público y la Policía Nacional, estableciendo mecanismos de sanción, por ejemplo, para aquellas personas que provoquen incendios forestales, tal y como dice la Ley N° 29263 artículo 310 del Código Penal Delito Contra los Bosques que condena entre 4 a 6 años y prestación de servicios comunitarios de 40 a 80 jornadas a quien “destruye, quema, daña o tala, bosques u otras formaciones boscosas”. Villarrubia asegura que el gobierno puede y debe llevar a cabo acciones de prevención para evitar que situaciones como esta se les escape de las manos: “ellos saben en qué época del año se da la quema de cultivos, debe haber una campaña progresiva de sensibilizar, capacitar para migrar a otros mecanismos (de cultivo), con monitoreo permanente y no esperar a que las cosas se salgan de control para recién intervenir”. Otro factor que no debemos dejar de lado es el tema ambiental, el impacto que tiene sobre la población local, pero también el ecosistema como las actividades productivas que se realizan en la zona afectada por este cúmulo de incendios. “Hay ovinos muertos, recién se están evaluando los daños para cuantificarlos. Cerca de 12 viviendas han sido quemadas por varios incendios forestales, pérdidas de cultivos. Hay que consolidar todo esto para tener un registro de qué tipos de cultivos son los que se han perdido”, acota Miguel Oscco, quien menciona que el efecto invernadero tiene repercusión en la deglaciación, la pérdida de agua como consecuencia directa de los incendios forestales. En ese sentido, la directora de Perú Resiliente propone como opción las fajas cortafuegos que, en los hechos, son pequeñas zanjas que se construyen para hacer las quemas, las cuales son claves para evitar que el fuego se expanda evitando que crezca: “esa es una manera para cortar los incendios forestales. Falta un acompañamiento técnico a los agricultores e insistir con campañas en medios de comunicación. Hay que llevar al personal de las instituciones públicas a estas zonas”. De acuerdo a lo expuesto por el director regional de la oficina de gestión de riesgo de desastres y seguridad, en lo que va del 2026, la región Cusco viene reportando unos 278 incendios forestales, casi a la par que en 2025, pero mucho menor que en 2020 o 2022. Asimismo, acota que este año se han visto afectadas alrededor de 8 mil hectáreas, pero con un total de 15 mil desde hace cuatro años. “En 2022 casi llegamos a 40 mil, pero nuestro trabajo está teniendo resultados reduciendo la tasa de hectáreas afectadas, pero también hemos sincerado la información”, detalló, además de insistir que el 100 por ciento de los incendios forestales reportados en 2026 en Cusco son producto de la intervención humana.

articles.title: Pretend you're sitting at Elizabeth Holmes' desk on this weirdly detailed website | TechCrunch
articles.summary: With over a thousand emails, slides, texts, and documents from the United States v. Elizabeth Holmes trial, Extend engineer Bo Lau created a website that simulates what it might have been like to rifle through the Theranos founder's desk.
articles.body_text: With over a thousand emails, slides, texts, and documents unveiled during the United States v. Elizabeth Holmes trial, Extend engineer Bo Lau created a website that simulates what it might have been like to be the chief executive of Theranos before everything came crashing down. (Every day, I am grateful to the American legal system for making the discovery process public.) i built a website where you can sit at elizabeth holmes’ desk open her macbook, scroll her iphone, run the theranos edison machine her texts, emails, slides, documents, and theranos machine records are real, sourced from exhibits in the united states v. holmes criminal trial pic.twitter.com/5At9T5m3UV The environment that Lau created is ambitiously detailed, taking you right back to 2016, a time when iPhones had home buttons, and you had to slide your finger across the screen to unlock it. Even the MacBook Air is running OS X El Capitan. You can click around the environment, which lets you look through the documents made public from the court case on Holmes’ iPhone and laptop screens. You can even run the Theranos Edison machine, the company’s ill-fated device that was supposed to be able to extract large amounts of health data from one drop of blood. The project seems like it was mostly made for laughs, but it’s actually an interesting way to peruse the documents from one of the most infamous court cases in tech history — it’s a lot easier to navigate this than to source thousands of PDFs from court websites. There’s another agenda, though. Lau is promoting a watch party that her company is throwing for Nathan Fielder’s upcoming documentary about Elizabeth Holmes, “ You Can See Everything .” Also, of course, she’s promoting the company itself. So, what exactly does Extend do? Apparently, it can “parse, extract, and split your hardest documents with unmatched accuracy.” (I’m not really sure what that means, but if it makes something like this Holmes desk simulator possible, then I guess that means I’m bullish on B2B SaaS.) articles.title: Fired OpenAI safety researchers dispute misconduct claims, warn of chilling effect | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Three fired OpenAI safety researchers dispute allegations of mishandling sensitive information, warning in an open letter that their dismissals are creating a chilling effect on the company’s AI safety culture.
articles.body_text: Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak, and Mikita Balesni, the three safety researchers that OpenAI fired last week , have published an open letter denying the firm’s claims that they mishandled sensitive information outside of established company procedures and warned that their dismissal signals a chilling effect that will have ripple effects across the company’s culture. “We have become concerned that internal and external communications around our firing have made our former colleagues afraid to speak and operate in ways that, until last week, were an integral part of working at OpenAI,” the researchers wrote Thursday in an open letter to OpenAI’s Safety and Security Committee, Safety Advisory Group, and Mission Advisory Council. The researchers were dismissed last week after allegedly sharing confidential company information with a third-party AI safety organization. OpenAI said they violated the company’s policies by “accessing and handling sensitive company information.” “AI is not a normal technology, and OpenAI is not a normal company,” Wang, Korbak, and Balesni wrote. “Those of us who work on safety see risks before anyone else, and we rely on close collaboration with outside experts to work out how to address them. The freedom to do so without fear, and to have well-defined internal procedures that enable this work, is itself an essential safety mechanism.” They said that their firing represents a broader shift in the culture of OpenAI, one that used to encourage workers to “raise safety concerns and disagree openly.” They said employees are now “unclear on where they stand” when behavior that was allegedly normal a month ago is now suddenly grounds for dismissal. “Given the significant safety concerns surrounding the development of AI, employees must not be left working in an environment where fear and unclear rules stymie AI safety work and weaken third-party accountability,” they wrote. “Terminations such as ours, executed and communicated so abruptly, are chilling the open culture OpenAI has prized in the past.” In the letter, the three denied involvement in a leak to The Information about less monitorable architectures in OpenAI’s newest models that make chain-of-thought reasoning more difficult to monitor. They also denied engaging with external parties outside the mandates of their jobs. OpenAI has not formally responded to the open letter, but shared with TechCrunch an internal memo attributed to a research leader, praising the three researchers’ contributions to AI safety and denying that they were fired in retaliation. “I want to be very clear that these decisions were not about raising safety concerns or speaking out,” the memo reads. “We have always encouraged that and always will. We do not terminate employees for raising concerns.” Separately, an OpenAI spokesperson told TechCrunch the three were fired after an investigation revealed a “pattern of misconduct” in “clear violation of our policies of mishandling research information” that goes beyond sharing information with an outside AI evaluation group. OpenAI did not directly address TechCrunch’s questions about specifically which policies the researchers allegedly violated, the circumstances of their dismissal, or how the company protects employees who raise safety concerns and collaborate with external evaluators. The firings have fueled speculation about their circumstances, particularly as OpenAI faces scrutiny over recent safety incidents involving rogue agents and leaks about its models.

articles.title: Ben Affleck is an AI nerd, and the internet is impressed | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Ben Affleck is going viral for his deep knowledge of AI, from neural networks and transformers to open weights. The actor, who sold his AI filmmaking startup to Netflix earlier this year, is proving he's more than just a Hollywood star.
articles.body_text: They cast the wrong lead in “Good Will Hunting,” apparently, because it’s Ben Affleck who is the secret genius, as it turns out. The actor who earlier this year sold his AI filmmaking startup to Netflix for a reported $587 million has gone viral this week for demonstrating his understanding of AI technology, neural networks, machine learning, and the like, across multiple video clips of his recent interviews. He can even write a little Python, he says. The movie star delved into his interest in technology most recently on an episode of GQ’s “One More Question” series this week, where he humbly started with “I’ve always been kind of into computers since I was young,” before nerding out on the development of AI as it relates to filmmaking, while using AI terminology like machine learning, neural networks, transformers, tensors, GPUs, inference, and more. In a clip that’s making the rounds, Affleck explains to the impressed interviewer, Zach Baron, that he got into the space when analog film moved to digital. As he spoke, he kept defining terms so the interviewer could understand what he was talking about. “I became more interested in that aspect of it, and the visual effects workflow for many years has included machine learning,” Affleck began. “So I can write, like, pretty shitty Python scripts and stuff like that. Because with convolutional neural networks — which were the sort of precursors to what the transformer can do — which is just much more computation simultaneously — you would do things like, look at what’s called a tensor — which is just the numerical translation of a visual image, in numbers like the batch number, the frame number, the red, green, and blue values of each pixel in each frame, and how many? It’s just that simple, right?” No, Ben Affleck, it is not just that simple, which is why this video is going viral. The actor then went into how neural networks were used to identify patterns and do edge detection or feature extraction, which he described as “identifying patterns enough to know — like this is where the window ledge is, so we can more easily take the green screen image out and replace it with something.” He also admitted he used his status as a Hollywood star to get a peek at emerging AI technology, at times. OpenAI was among those he visited, Affleck said in a separate clip, which ultimately led him to understand how he could get more directly involved in the AI space. As the interviewer continued, Affleck explained how AI can help with filmmaking while not replacing it, leading to the development and sale of his own startup in this space. (He claims the $587 million figure is “not right,” noting that he didn’t own the whole company.) “I gambled on this notion that in order to do this in an ethical way and in a way that could take this technology and actually make it work hand in glove with artists in this community where there are very fixed, long-standing relationships around likeness and so forth, we had to create our own dataset,” he said. “So I raised the money. I shot for about eight months with a lot of cameras and a lot of equipment, and created a dataset that would serve as late-stage training for open models to do discrete tasks, sort of where the training code, the inference code, were related to one another and geared toward actual specific tasks that would generate value,” Affleck said. In a separate clip, also going viral, Affleck spoke to Bloomberg’s Lucas Shaw at the Screentime 2026 conference in LA, where he talked about how he fine-tuned AI models by taking open source models, unfreezing the weights, then teaching them to meet certain cinematic standards. In the process, the filmmaker retains their proprietary work, while benefiting from the learning they create by training their own unique model for the movie they’re making. articles.title: Popular AI leaderboard Arena nearly doubles valuation to $3.1B valuation in 10 months | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The company behind the popular LMArena leaderboard has raised $200 million led by Lightspeed and Khosla, and is now measuring AI models on alignment issues such as lying.
articles.body_text: Arena , which originated in 2023 as a research project at UC Berkeley that crowdsourced rankings of AI models, has raised a $200 million Series B round at a $3.1 billion valuation, it said on Thursday. This comes after the company said it reached $100 million in annualized run-rate revenue in June. The round was led by Lightspeed Venture Partners and Khosla Ventures, with Salesforce Ventures, 01 Advisors, Dell Technologies Capital, Endeavor Catalyst, a16z, Felicis, and others joining in. Arena previously announced a $150 million Series A in January at a $1.7 billion post-money valuation. At the time, its annualized revenue was $30 million , it said. So that means its valuation has nearly doubled in about 10 months. Arena provides a crowdsourced platform that is free for consumers to use. People enter prompts or request vibe-coded projects and then rate which model does it better. Arena claims it has tens of millions of monthly visitors. In September of last year, it introduced its commercial product, AI Evaluations , a service that provides model labs and enterprises with detailed performance analytics based on its community feedback. The timing proved impeccable. This year, AI labs realized that their models were gaming benchmarking tests, finding ways to rack up good scores without truly earning them. At the same time, enterprises wanted help determining which model works best for their own internal needs rather than relying only on standardized benchmarks. “AI is advancing faster than our ability to evaluate it, and static benchmarks break down once models recognize they’re being tested,” the company said in its funding announcement. “The world needs a neutral third party to measure how safe and aligned AI actually is once it’s in the hands of real people. Arena is stepping into that role today,” it added. To that end, Arena has also added a new category to its leaderboard: alignment . This is where it ranks models based on issues like unauthorized action (taking actions it wasn’t asked to take); false attribution (wrongly crediting statements or facts to the wrong source); and what it calls “deceptive completion” (lying about completing tasks that it didn’t do). Currently, a slate of OpenAI’s models are at the top of its preliminary alignment leaderboard, with Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Fable in sixth and ninth place, respectively. articles.title: OpenAI's math solutions aren't meeting the field's standards yet | TechCrunch
articles.summary: OpenAI's flood of proofs deviated from the guidelines set by a group of mathematical researchers consulted by the frontier lab.
articles.body_text: When OpenAI released hundreds of claimed solutions to some of the world’s hardest math problems this week, the frontier lab said that it had consulted an advisory group of elite mathematicians to avoid the controversy that came with the last time one of its models solved a long-standing problem in the field. But OpenAI fell short of those standards, particularly where the mathematicians emphasized the need for human understanding of a mathematical result. That’s especially concerning after a new paper highlighted gaps between the natural language and formally expressed solution to a million-dollar problem ostensibly solved by OpenAI’s models. The Advisory Group on Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence (AGMAI), hosted by Princeton University’s Institute for Advanced Studies, is made up of nine prominent researchers at institutions around the world. The organization released guidelines for frontier labs solving math problems at the end of September. In a statement on the latest set of proofs, the AGMAI said that “it is ultimately up to the mathematical community to assess the extent to which our recommendations were followed successfully.” However, the organization’s first request was “to stop testing advanced mathematical problems on proprietary models.” OpenAI’s release explicitly says that it is evaluating its proprietary models using open research problems in mathematics. The advisory group did not respond when asked by TechCrunch for a more thorough evaluation of OpenAI’s latest proof release. The lab clearly followed some of its principles, including releasing results as soon as possible and including information about how the models reached their conclusions. But not for all of them: Just 10 of the 719 manuscripts included releases of the model’s chain of thought. For papers that people don’t understand, the mathematicians suggested the proofs should be formalized — but just 42% of the proofs released by OpenAI had not undergone this process. Ultimately, it’s still not clear that OpenAI is taking “responsibility for ensuring that human understanding will follow” when releasing its proofs, in accordance to the AGMAI principles. AGMAI suggested that OpenAI should help fund the work of human mathematicians who will be required to make the lab’s solutions meaningful in any real way. “Problems are being solved autonomously by AI prompters who have no interest in the broader field itself once their initial target is ‘solved’, and do not understand the AI output well enough to answer questions on the result, give talks, or otherwise interact with the rest of the field,” Terence Tao, a prominent mathematician who has criticized OpenAI’s approach, wrote on social media after the release. That problem is exemplified by a paper released this week by mathematicians at the University of Cambridge and King’s College in London that questions the way frontier labs are approaching these challenges. When AI models solve mathematical problems, they first create a “natural language” explanation, then try to express that result in Lean, a programming language that in theory confirms the accuracy of the proof by compiling it as code. However, there may be problems with the way the models translate their natural language proofs into code; this paper documents at least two discrepancies between the natural language proof and the Lean code behind the solution OpenAI has offered to a problem derived from the Navier-Stokes equations that describe the complex behavior of fluids.

articles.title: US bars Microsoft, Adobe, and major IT firms from green card program for skilled foreign workers | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The other firms being suspended from the program include Capgemini, Cognizant, HCL, Infosys, Tata, and Wipro.
articles.body_text: The Trump administration is suspending Microsoft, Adobe, and several other technology companies from a program that helps skilled foreign workers obtain permanent residency in the United States, accusing the companies of fraud. “Our ​message to Microsoft is: You’re a great American company, ​but you’ve got to hire great American workers,” U.S. ⁠Vice President JD Vance said in a news conference on Thursday, Reuters reported. The other firms being suspended from the program include Capgemini, Cognizant, HCL, Infosys, Tata, and Wipro. Secretary of Labor Keith Sonderling said the government would not accept any new or pending permanent ​labor certification applications involving these companies. H-1B visas are designed for highly skilled positions that employers may struggle to fill with qualified U.S. workers. Tech companies are among the largest users of the program, with nearly three-quarters of approved visas going to workers from India, according to The Associated Press . “We believe in the strength and talent of the American workforce,” a Microsoft spokesperson said in an email to TechCrunch. “That is why the vast majority of Microsoft employees in the United States are Americans. We look forward to providing the Administration with additional information. For example, of the approximately 6,000 H-1B visa applications we submitted in the last fiscal year, 80% percent were to extend or change the status of existing Microsoft employees.” The statement continues, “These were not to hire new people. The remaining filings for new employees were for individuals already legally in the United States who decided to come work for us, and they equal only 1% of our U.S. workforce. They are not new arrivals to our country.” The company went on to note that it only files H-1B petitions for those who meet the “rigorous standards” of the visa category, and that pays its H-1B employees the same as any “other employees doing comparable work.” Vance also said during the news conference that the administration would investigate nine universities, including Harvard, Yale, and Stanford, over allegations they’re abusing a program that allows international students to come to the U.S. and were using the program to undermine wages for American workers. Adobe did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Update 10/08/2026 1:50pm ET: The article was updated to include a statement from Microsoft. articles.title: Cal AI's 19-year-old founder just raised $10M for his new AI startup | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Zach Yadegari, the teen co-founder of popular Cal AI calorie tracking app, has launched a new personal AI agent startup that competes with Instinct, Muse, and Bee.
articles.body_text: Zach Yadegari, the teen co-founder of calorie tracking app Cal AI, has launched Persona , a new AI agent startup, and already raised $10 million. Vine Ventures led the round, with Z Fellows founder Cory Levy and Collective Global participating. In March, MyFitnessPal acquired Cal AI for an undisclosed sum after it zoomed ahead of the older calorie app in the app store rankings. The deal was big enough to convince Yadegari and his co-founders to sell the company after it had pulled in over $30 million in annual revenue in under two years, MyFitnessPal told TechCrunch at the time. Yadegari and his co-founders originally went to work for their new owner, continuing development on Cal AI, but he left the bigger company in June, he tells TechCrunch. He then went right to work on his next idea. (He is working with another co-founder who has yet to be announced.) That idea is Persona , a personal AI assistant similar to Instinct or Meta’s Muse but with a hardware component that will soon be available: a $179 wearable band. That makes Persona somewhat more like Bee, the wearable AI device that Amazon acquired in 2025 , but Persona’s device differs in several ways, Yadegari tells TechCrunch. For one, it won’t be ambient AI, meaning it won’t always be listening and recording. The band will have a button that activates the assistant, or it can be set up to activate with the flick of one’s wrist. In this way, it is promising that user conversations stay private and cannot be sold to advertisers or data brokers. The team is also baking in safeguards to protect the assistant against phishing and prompt-injection attempts, Yadegari says. These are two areas that can plague agents, say AI labs like OpenAI. Plus, he promises that Persona’s agent can’t see a user’s credit-card details and that purchases will require the user’s approval, with payment handled through external providers such as Stripe Link. Link is Stripe’s secure wallet designed for use by agents. Although user data won’t be sold to advertisers, the startup’s current business model does rely on ads. Yadegari says the company will show advertised wares during shopping research. But he says that the agent will present unbiased recommendations because the agent won’t know which of the items are advertised. For example, if someone is researching office chairs, he says, “the agent knows their preferences” and will show them chairs that match those preferences, some of them sponsored results. The bands are expected to be available in December, and an app is in the works. In the meantime, Persona has launched as a free beta product in which users work with the assistant via iMessage text messages. It has attracted “a few thousand beta users,” Yadegari said. The band has also already generated “five figures in preorder revenue.” Like other consumer AI assistants, he says, Persona can order food or rides, take notes, book travel, answer questions and emails, among other tasks. “All of the utility apps that you use on your phone day-to-day, whether those are apps for shopping, whether it’s Uber, DoorDash, your email — these are all collapsing and will collapse into a single super app powered by an AI assistant,” Yadegari said.

articles.title: Not even Spotify is safe from AI slop
articles.summary: Artists such as Standards, Health, Annie, and Swans have had AI-generated albums that aren’t theirs showing up on their Spotify pages. Why?
articles.body_text: I first noticed something weird when a HEALTH album dropped on my Spotify new release radar. Except the cover design was funny — it didn’t look like a HEALTH album. And it wasn’t. [Image: A screenshot of the fake Annie album, taken October 12th. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/25732450/Screenshot_2024_10_12_at_4.23.09_PM.png?quality=90&strip=all] Some kind of AI slop had been uploaded to HEALTH’s artist page on Spotify, one of three fake albums that would appear under their name that weekend. The band’s X account made some jokes about it, the albums were eventually removed, and I went back to minding my own business. Then, the next weekend, I saw a new Annie album had dropped. That album was more plausible — Annie had just released a new single, “The Sky Is Blue” — but when I clicked in, I couldn’t find it on the list of the song titles. Confused, I played the album and heard birdsong and a vaguely New Age-y instrumental. That… did not sound like Annie. So I did what any normal person would do: I bitched about it in my group chat. Which was how I heard that this was happening to other artists, like a lot of artists, and had been happening for months. (“I get one of these in my release radar often,” my buddy Gordon said.) For a while, metalcore artists such as Caliban, Northlane, and Silent Planet had been targeted. But so had a lot of artists with single-word names, such as Swans, Asia, Standards, and Gong. A new album would appear on an artist’s Spotify page, bearing their name but no similarity to their music. Sometimes, as with the fake HEALTH albums, they would disappear after a few days. Other times, they would linger indefinitely, even against the artist’s will. [Image: Can you spot the fake? https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/25732455/Screenshot_2024_10_15_at_12.48.26_PM.png?quality=90&strip=all] “It was super weird,” says Marcos Mena, Standards’ lead songwriter and guitarist. “I thought, ‘Oh, this is something Spotify will take care of.’” After all, Standards has a verified artist page. But when a fake album was posted on September 26th, it didn’t budge. Mena emailed Spotify to tell them there’d been a mistake. The streamer responded two weeks later, on October 8th: “It looks like the content is mapped correctly to the artist’s page. If you require further assistance, please contact your music provider. Please do not reply to this message.” As of November 8th, the fake Standards album was still right there under the band’s verified, blue-checked name. It was finally removed by November 11th. “That was upsetting to me, because if you have ears, you can definitely hear it’s not our music,” Mena told me. “It’s definitely a bummer because we did have a new album come out this year, and I feel like it’s detracting from that.” What if someone came to a concert where Standards was opening for another band, went to Spotify to check out more tunes, and got the fake album instead? [Image: Can you spot the fake? https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/25732473/Screenshot_2024_11_08_at_3.26.43_PM.png?quality=90&strip=all] To me, this all raised an obvious question: fucking why? Given the history of scams on Spotify, I think the answer is money. (The answer is almost always money.) To understand how this works, you need a sense of the mechanics. Streaming platforms like Spotify don’t work like your Facebook page — Mena and other artists aren’t logging in and adding albums to their accounts directly. Instead, they go through a distributor that handles licensing, metadata, and royalty payments. Distributors send songs and metadata in bulk to the streaming services. The metadata part is important; it includes things such as the song title and artist name but also other information, such as the songwriter, record label, and so on. This is crucial for artists (and others) to get paid. But this whole process effectively works on the honor system, and for something like the fake Standards album, this is where the problems begin. A distributor takes you at your word that you are who you say you are, Spotify takes the distributor at their word, and boom, there’s a fake album on a real artist’s page. Most of the time when this happens, it’s an honest mistake. In the recent spate of fakes, though, it seems like artists are directly targeted. Because the money an artist receives for streams goes through the distributor, the fake Standards album — should it get any payout at all — will reward someone other than Mena. We know the real Standards are on Topshelf Records, but the fake appears to be on something called Gupta Music, so Standards’ real label isn’t getting a cut, either. If enough people stream the album, the royalties will flow straight to Gupta Music… along with the payout from hundreds of other releases full of slop. Mena said he’d filed with his distributor to have the fake Standards album taken down. But whoever did it — Spotify or his distributor — didn’t notify Mena; I did, when I asked if he’d been involved in the removal. He wasn’t, he texted me, “but yayyyyy someone did something.” Going to Every Noise at Once — essentially an encyclopedia of what’s on Spotify — and searching for Gupta Music, I saw more than 700 releases. The cover art looked remarkably similar and smacked of AI. The purported band names were mostly one word: “Rany,” “Living,” “Bedroom,” and “Culture.” The albums shared names with the faux bands. A search for “Gupta Music” returned only a 14-year-old TED Talk by a man named Robert Gupta. [Image: Screenshot of Every Noise at Once, before the albums were removed. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/25732478/Screenshot_2024_10_31_at_1.36.06_PM.png?quality=90&strip=all] Even the supposed label name struck me as suspicious. There’s a well-known marketing agency called Gupta Media. It reps entertainment companies including Disney Music Group, Republic Records (in service of The Weeknd’s album), and Sony Music. In an email to The Verge, Gupta Media spokesperson Carly Carioli confirmed the agency “has no connection” to Gupta Music. “To be clear, Gupta Media is not now nor have we ever been involved in any of the activity you’re addressing — i.e., uploading fake music by fake artists to the profiles of real artists,” said Carioli. It looks like Standards, Annie, HEALTH, Swans, and a number of other notable one-word artists were targeted directly. Spotify confirmed that the onslaught of AI garbage was delivered from one source, the licensor Ameritz Music. Ameritz Music did not respond to a request for comment. “Due to significant and repeated violations of Spotify’s Metadata Style Guide, we ended our relationship with the licensor that provided the content in question,” said Chris Macowski, Spotify’s global head of music communication, in an emailed statement. “As a result, the content was removed from our platform.” Macowski also said that Spotify “invests heavily in automated and manual reviews” to prevent royalty fraud. Earlier attempts focused on metalcore musicians such as Fit for an Autopsy, Alpha Wolf, and Like Moths to Flames also seem like a coordinated attempt to siphon off legitimate streams. The culprit in that case was Vibratech Musicians, according to Idioteq. Each individual payout for a song stream on Spotify is tiny, as legitimate musicians who use the platform frequently lament. But hundreds or thousands of songs with relatively modest streaming numbers, when combined, can lead to big payouts. A fraudster just has to upload music and find a way to make accounts play it. And this doesn’t just happen on Spotify. There are more than 100 streaming platforms where artists can run this scam. In early November, Universal Music Group (UMG) sued Believe, a music distributor, and its US subsidiary TuneCore. In that lawsuit, UMG alleges Believe has a “conscious business strategy of indiscriminately distributing and purporting to license tracks with full knowledge that many of the clients of its distribution services are fraudsters.” The suit is about copyright infringement, and the details in it are striking. UMG alleges that artists such as “Kendrik Laamar,” “Arriana Gramde,” “Jutin Biber,” and “Llady Gaga” are among those Believe uploaded — suggesting a strategy of attempting to capture streams from users who had simply typoed. Another strategy is creating AI covers of popular songs and getting them onto popular playlists so normal people will stream them. Another involves bots “listening” to songs. Earlier this year, a Danish man was sentenced to 18 months in prison for using bots to get about $300,000 in royalties. Another man, Michael Smith, was arrested and charged with defrauding streaming services out of $10 million over the course of seven years. Smith used AI tools to create hundreds of thousands of songs under the names of fake artists such as “Calm Baseball,” “Calm Connected,” and “Calm Knuckles.” He then streamed the huge catalog using bots, billions of times, prosecutors allege. That diverted money that should have gone to real musicians that real people were really listening to. (In this case, Spotify paid only $60,000 to Smith, suggesting the company’s protective measures worked to limit payments, Macowski said.) “People upload massive amounts of albums that are intended to be streaming fraud albums,” says Andrew Batey, the CEO of Beatdapp, a company that aims to prevent streaming fraud. Batey estimates that $2 billion to $3 billion is stolen from artists through this kind of fraud every year. Distribution plays a big role. Most distributors’ business models are based on getting a cut of whatever royalties come back to the artists and labels. “Even though they may not be participating in the fraud, they directly benefit from it,” Batey says. In its suit, UMG alleges that Believe “wrongfully collects royalties it knows are properly payable by digital music services” such as UMG on copyrighted material. A sophisticated fraud operation will use multiple fake labels and multiple distributors in order to avoid having a single point of failure. Besides bot accounts, a number of bad actors have access to real people’s compromised accounts. “They log in as you and me, play their song three times and leave,” Batey says. That fake stream is then hidden among all the real listening the real account is doing. Gupta Music wasn’t the only label I found doing bulk uploading. There were three more doing something similar: Future Jazz Records, Ancient Lake Records, and Beat Street Music. All had also uploaded hundreds of albums with AI-looking album art. It’s unclear how these labels intended to generate streams, if at all. By the time of publication, most of those albums had been removed. Problems with metadata have existed for years — some of them innocent, some considerably less so. “We’ve basically gotten lucky so far,” says Glenn McDonald, a former Spotify employee who runs Every Noise at Once. “The content validation system without any input on the artist level is fairly crazy.” When something goes wrong, there are two levels where it can be addressed: the streaming service and the distributor. Distributors have to strike a delicate balance. They make their money by getting a cut of the streaming payout. If they are too aggressive in policing the uploads, legitimate artists get caught. Fixing that is expensive, and distribution is a low-margin, bulk business, McDonald says. But allowing too many junk bands through creates problems with the streaming services. As for the streaming services, they usually have data that could allow them to sort this out. If, for instance, the distributor that usually uploads Standards albums isn’t the one used for the new album, that’s the kind of thing that could be used to flag the album for review. (So is the change in label.) McDonald told me he also built tools for Spotify to identify when a song doesn’t sound like the rest of an artist’s catalog. Sometimes that can happen for legitimate reasons; an EDM remix of an Ed Sheeran song isn’t going to sound like Ed Sheeran, but it may still have happened with the label’s and artist’s approval. Also, some legitimate artists share the same name, especially tiny indie bands, and they just have separate pages. “The way it should have worked, getting the plumbing right, is that all those albums should have been flagged as new artists, and then it wouldn’t matter,” McDonald told me. As for the distributors, the thing to keep an eye on is UMG’s lawsuit. A pretrial conference is scheduled for January. The outcome of the suit could potentially change how distributors filter the music people try to upload through their platforms — because if lawsuits are more expensive than content moderation, there’s likely to be more content moderation. That could improve things for Spotify, which is downstream of them. Just banning AI-generated content from Spotify — or distributors — might feel like an intuitive solution. But despite the backlash against AI-generated media, there are legitimate AI-generated songs. For instance, “10 Drunk Cigarettes,” from Girly Girl Productions, is something of a hit. (It also is likely human-assisted, rather than wholly AI-generated.) UMG has made a deal with Soundlabs to allow artists to use Soundlabs’ AI vocals for themselves. It’s also partnered with Klay Vision to create a model for generating music. Besides, AI is just an accelerant for a type of fraud that’s lived on Spotify for years, says Batey. Fraudsters used to dig up old, obscure albums and digitize them or slightly alter a song that already existed. AI has just cut down on the amount of work that’s required to make the fake song needed to get the streaming money. At the same time… accelerants sure do make things burn down faster. Plenty of platforms have become less useful as they’ve been choked with AI glurge — Facebook, Instagram, the artist formerly known as Twitter, even Google itself. AI music poses the same threat to Spotify, McDonald says. He points out that I had been waiting for the Annie album, excited for it, even. And then instead, I got duped into garbage. “There’s all these mechanisms around assuming this stuff is correct,” he says. But right now, those mechanisms are broken — and people who truly care, like artists themselves, don’t have their hands on the controls. Update November 15th: Adds emailed statement from Gupta Media. Correction November 15th: The original version of this story referred to Carly Carioli as a spokeswoman. Carioli uses he/him pronouns.

articles.title: Google’s invisible AI watermark will help identify generative text and video
articles.summary: Google DeepMind’s SynthID can now watermark AI-generated video and text. It’s one of several standards alongside C2PA.
articles.body_text: Among Google’s swath of new AI models and tools announced today, the company is also expanding its AI content watermarking and detection technology to work across two new mediums. Google’s DeepMind CEO, Demis Hassabis, took the stage for the first time at the Google I/O developer conference on Tuesday to talk not only about the team’s new AI tools, like the Veo video generator, but also about the new upgraded SynthID watermark imprinting system. It can now mark video that was digitally generated as well as AI-generated text. Watermarking AI-generated content will matter increasingly as the technology gains prevalence, especially when AI gets used for malicious purposes. It’s already been used to spread political misinformation, claim someone said something they haven’t, and create nonconsensual sexual content. SynthID was announced last August and started as a tool to imprint AI imagery in a way that humans can’t visually decipher — but can be detected by the system. The approach is different from other aspiring watermarking protocol standards like C2PA, which adds cryptographic metadata to AI-generated content. Google had also enabled SynthID to inject inaudible watermarks into AI-generated music that was made using DeepMind’s Lyria model. SynthID is just one of several AI safeguards in development to combat misuse by the tech, safeguards that the Biden administration is directing federal agencies to build guidelines around. articles.title: Google’s Gemini AI is coming to the sidebar in Docs, Drive, Gmail, and more
articles.summary: Google’s AI assistant will now work across its productivity apps, and Gemini can help you do everything from write emails to save events to your calendar.
articles.body_text: The right sidebar in Google’s Workspace apps is now the center for a lot of Google’s AI plans. The company announced today at its I/O developer conference that it is bringing Gemini 1.5 Pro, its latest mainstream language model, to the sidebar in Google Docs, Sheets, Slides, Drive, and Gmail. It’ll be the same virtual assistant across all of those apps, and the key bit is that it’ll know about everything you have saved everywhere. The idea seems to be to use Gemini to connect all the Workspace apps more seamlessly. According to Aparna Pappu, the general manager and VP of Workspace, Google users have long been trying to hack Gemini to do complicated, multi-app things: send an email based on the data they’re looking at in Sheets or add a reminder to respond to the email they were currently looking at. And since Gemini has access to all of your documents, emails, and files, it can answer questions without forcing you to switch apps. In a briefing with press ahead of I/O, Pappu gave the example of searching for information about a New York Knicks game. “I could ask something like, ‘what time do doors open for the Knicks game,’ and I’m not looking for information from the web, which is going to give me generic information. I want information from my ticket, which happens to be a PDF in my email somewhere.” Gemini can find that information, and Pappu said early users are quickly learning to use it as a way to find things more quickly. Among early testers, Pappu said, a popular use case has been receipts. Rather than dig through your email, your files, and everything, you can just ask Gemini to find and organize all your receipts from across your Google account. “And let’s say you hit on the prompt that says ‘Put my expenses in a Drive folder,’” she says, “from there Gemini can put them all into a Sheet.” In keeping with so many of Google’s announcements at I/O, the Workspace team seems to be focused on using Gemini to help you get stuff done — and do stuff on your behalf. Pappu talked about how popular Gmail’s “Help me write” feature has been, especially on mobile, where people don’t want to type as much. By grounding the model in your data and not the entire internet, Google hopes it can also begin to mitigate the model’s tendency to hallucinate and make other mistakes. At least for now, the new sidebar isn’t for everyone: it’s available now to some early testers and will roll out to paid Gemini subscribers next month. But Pappu did say Google is looking at how it could use on-device models to bring the capabilities to more users over time, so your days of hunting through Google Drive to find that old PDF may finally be coming to an end. articles.title: The FCC bans robocalls with AI-generated voices
articles.summary: The Federal Communications Commission has banned the use of AI-generated voices in robocalls. A ruling issued on Thursday makes the voices illegal.
articles.body_text: The Federal Communications Commission is making it illegal for robocalls to use AI-generated voices. The ruling, issued on Thursday, gives state attorneys general the ability to take action against callers using AI voice cloning tech. As outlined in the ruling, AI-generated voices are now considered “an artificial or prerecorded voice” under the Telephone Consumer Protection Act (TCPA). This restricts callers from using AI-generated voices for non-emergency purposes or without prior consent. The TCPA includes bans on a variety of automated call practices, including using an “artificial or prerecorded voice” to deliver messages, but it wasn’t explicitly stated whether this included AI-powered voice cloning. The new ruling clarifies that these recordings should indeed fall under the law’s scope. “Bad actors are using AI-generated voices in unsolicited robocalls to extort vulnerable family members, imitate celebrities, and misinform voters,” FCC Chairwoman Jessica Rosenworcel said in a statement. “State Attorneys General will now have new tools to crack down on these scams and ensure the public is protected from fraud and misinformation.” Although state attorneys general could already go after the bad actors behind robocalls based on the scam or fraud they’re perpetrating, this new ruling gives them the power to hold scam artists accountable solely because they’re using an AI-generated voice. The FCC first proposed banning the use of AI voices in robocalls last month. Scrutiny of AI voices in robocalls has ramped up in recent weeks. In January, some New Hampshire residents received a call that appeared to use AI to impersonate President Joe Biden’s voice, and it told them not to show up at the polls for the state’s presidential primary. An investigation has since linked the robocall to two Texas-based companies: Life Corporation and Lingo Telecom. The FCC issued a cease-and-desist order to Lingo Telecom, which transmitted the call.

articles.title: Trump: Säger du ordet så är du min fiende
articles.summary: Trump betraktar alla som använder uttrycket ”AI” och ”artificiell intelligens” som ”fienden”. Så lyder presidentens nya hot.
articles.body_text: Trump betraktar alla som använder uttrycket ”AI” och ”artificiell intelligens” som ”fienden”. Så lyder presidentens nya hot enligt Politico . Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Federala myndigheter i USA beordrades nyligen att hänvisa till AI som ”superintelligens” och ”SI” i offentlig kommunikation, på webbplatser, i rapporter och annat material. ”De extraordinära teknologier som amerikanska innovatörer banar väg för överträffar vida vad man föreställde sig när termen 'artificiell intelligens' först användes”, stod det i ordern. Denna order kom efter att president Donald Trump förra månaden gjorde en opinionsundersökning bland allmänheten om ett namnbyte eftersom han ansåg att uttrycken artificiell intelligens och AI ”är felaktiga och väldigt otydliga”. Han menade att superintelligens eller SI ”är en mycket mer elegant och korrekt beskrivning av fenomenet”. Trump skärpte tonläget kring detta i ett inlägg på Truth Social under torsdagen: ”Vita huset betraktar alla som använder termen ’artificiell intelligens’, i stället för den nya, mer korrekta och allmänt accepterade termen ”superintelligens”, som fienden.” Vita huset har tagit bort alla omnämnanden av AI och ersatt dem med SI på sin sajt om detta – men den heter fortfarande ai.gov. Trump har sedan tidigare försökt döpa om Mexikanska golfen till Amerikanska golfen och Lake Ontario till Lake America. Detta är en nyhetsartikel. articles.summary: Två döda kroppar har hittats på Teneriffa. En av dem beskrivs som ”mumifierad”.
articles.body_text: Två döda kroppar har hittats på Teneriffa. En av dem beskrivs som ”mumifierad”, skriver Canarian Weekly . Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Det var i helgen som en fotgängare larmade polisen efter att ha gjort ett makabert fynd vid en stig i ett område nära en motorväg på södra Teneriffa . När polisen anlände till platsen kunde de konstatera att det som hittats var en manskropp i ”ett avancerat mumifieringsstadium”. Området spärrades av i samband med utredningen. En obduktion kommer att genomföras för att försöka fastställa mannens identitet, dödsorsak. de exakta omständigheterna kring hans död och hur länge hans kvarlevor har funnits på platsen. Man fann inga uppenbara tecken på våld, men man inväntar resultaten av den rättsmedicinska undersökningen. I helgen hittades ytterligare en manskropp vid kusten vid Arona på södra Teneriffa. Polisen har inte sagt att det skulle finnas något samband mellan de två fallen. Detta är en nyhetsartikel. Expressen granskar, avslöjar och ger dig senaste nyheterna på ett sakligt sätt. Det var strax före klockan 18 på onsdagen som en maskerad person tog sig in på plastikkirurgkliniken Cirumed i Marbella på den spanska solkusten. Enligt spanska El País sökte gärningsmannen upp klinikens grundare, den 57-årige tyske plastikkirurgen Alexander Aslani, och sköt honom i huvudet flera gånger. Skytten flydde sedan från platsen, först till fots och därefter på motorcykel tillsammans med en misstänkt medhjälpare. När ambulanspersonal kom fram var Aslani fortfarande vid liv, men han avled senare av sina skador. På torsdagseftermiddagen greps en 18-årig svensk man misstänkt för mordet. Vad som ligger bakom dådet är ännu oklart. Enligt El País hade läkaren nyligen mottagit hot och polisen undersöker bland annat om mordet kan ha koppling till en missnöjd patient. Enligt brittiska The Sun finns misstankar om att det kan röra sig om ett beställningsmord. Alexander Aslani var en av Marbellas mest välkända plastikkirurger. Han grundade kliniken för över tio år sedan och hade över 200 000 följare på Instagram. Kliniken specialiserade sig bland annat på kroppsskulptering, fettsugning och så kallade Brazilian Butt Lifts. Enligt The Sun hade Aslani utfört över 15 000 operationer och lockat patienter från fler än 40 länder. Han hade tidigare även arbetat som överläkare i plastikkirurgi vid sjukhus i Storbritannien.

articles.title: Slarv med det hon köpte blev tolvåriga Mias död
articles.summary: Mia Shay St Hilaire köpte en milkshake. Det blev den tolvåriga flickans död.

På torsdagen fortsatte attackerna, när 33 människor dödades i en bussattack i ukrainska Kramatorsk. Om man ska tro tankesmedjan Institute for the Study of War är det här bara början på de ryska attackerna. ”Ryssland har för avsikt att göra livet svårare för civila genom att öka brutaliteten och dödligheten i attackerna”, skriver de i sin senaste rapport. Natten mellan 6 och 7 oktober avfyrade Ryssland 84 vanliga attackdrönare, 48 kryssningsrobotar och 46 jetdrönare. Enligt ISW har Ukraina svårt att skjuta ner jetdrönarna, som kan nå hastigheter upp till 900 kilometer i timmen. articles.title: Semesterchocken – blev enormt dyr

articles.body_text: Den blev en ”katastrof” som resulterade i en allvarlig skada och kostade tvåbarnsmamman en enorm summa, skriver Mirror . – Jag kommer aldrig att åka utomlands igen, säger Diane. articles.title: GPS-data visar sista minuten innan olyckan
articles.summary: Det är fortfarande oklart varför buss 845 körde av vägen. Men bussens GPS-data visar en plötslig förändring precis innan olyckan. Sekunder senare ligger bussen i diket. En ung man dog. – Vi ser en förändring, säger åklagaren.

En dubbeldäckarbuss med ett 40-tal passagerare ombord körde i diket mellan Växjö och Alvesta på måndagseftermiddagen. En man i 18-årsåldern omkom och ett tiotal skadades allvarligt. Chauffören har sedan olyckan suttit anhållen misstänkt för vållande till annans död, vållande till kroppsskada och vårdslöshet i trafik, men släpptes under torsdagsförmiddagen. Åklagaren Tommy Sköld säger att chauffören har lämnat sin förklaring och att misstankarna inte har skärpts under anhållandetiden. Vad misstankarna baserar sig på är oklart och polisutredningen är fortfarande i ett tidigt skede. Men genom den öppna GPS-data som bussen lämnat efter sig går det att följa sekunderna innan dödsolyckan skedde. Under rutten som startade klockan 16.15 i Växjö rapporterade bussens GPS-system automatiskt in position och hastighet ungefär varannan sekund.
